details.label: Discussion
details.text: A loosely organized band of thunderstorms is tracking southeastward across Lake Erie -- ahead of a midlevel vort max rotating around a deep upper low over southeastern Ontario. While cool surface temperatures downstream may limit the overall severe risk, steepened low-level lapse rates, enhanced unidirectional low/midlevel flow, and the strengthening cold pool may support a couple strong to locally damaging wind gusts across parts of northeastern OH and northwestern PA

details.label: Summary
details.text: Severe gusts remain possible across portions of MT this evening. Ongoing storms may gradually evolve into a linear or cluster or two later this evening

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Across WW 617 and 620, several clusters of strong to severe storms remain ongoing this evening. The air mass downstream is hot and sufficiently unstable to support the ongoing storms. Some CAM guidance and radar trends suggest some upscale growth into one or more clusters is possible this evening. This appears most likely across northern portions of MT where more robust convection is ongoing. Stronger vertical shear may also support better organization of these storms with time. With steep lapse rates in the lowest several km, severe gusts remain likely this evening

details.label: Summary
details.text: Severe wind gusts and hail remain possible with strong to severe storms across UT/ID and far western WY this evening

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Across WW 619, a band of strong to severe storms have matured across eastern ID with more isolated strong storms ongoing over northwest UT late this afternoon. A modestly moist, hot and moderately unstable air mas remains in place ahead of these storms which should continue to support them over the next several hours. Steep low-level lapse rates will primarily favor severe wind gusts, but enhanced mid-level flow at the base of the northern Rockies upper trough is supporting some cellular structures. Hail is possible, especially with any persistent supercells. Expectations are for convection to gradually spread northeastward across UT and far southwestern WY into this evening. Some clustering is possible, based on recent CAM solutions. This appears most likely over northern UT into southwest WY. This could support a localized corridor of more concentrated severe wind gusts later this evening. Given the ongoing storms and a generally favorable environment, the severe risk continues for much of WW619
